newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki stocks ease in stagnant trade.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki stocks ease in stagnant trade.

text.p: Shares were mired in negative ground on Monday with trade almost stagnant after U.S. stocks paused on Friday, and brokers said the trend would remain soft pending a new impetus from overseas.
"This is stagnant," one broker said, adding: "Prices could go a bit lower, but I don't see any big selling either."
Merita weighed down the index, falling 0.50 markka to 23.70, paring some of its recent sharp gains.
Nokia's liquid A share was a shade firmer, up 0.60 markka at 450.50 in slack 50 million markka trade, while the less-traded K share fell 5.00 markka to 450.00 in thin volume.
Amer advanced 3.50 markka to 91.50 in lively 17 million markka volume on the otherwise quiet bourse.

Brokers said the share was rising on position-taking ahead of a decision expected this week from Amer's board on whether it will redeem vote-heavy K shares sold at end-June to British investor Johathan Bryan Guinness, third Lord Moyne.
One newspaper said the deadline for the decision could be Wednesday, Saturday or Sunday, but the company said it had not yet decided when its board would convene.
Finnair reversed early gains, falling 0.40 markka to 43.50. --Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 235
